decision: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING: C4 fails (eta-squared=0.000 < 0.10 threshold). C1 passes (CV=0.584 > 0.10), C2 passes (7/21 pairs outside convex hull, threshold 3), C3 passes (|rho(hier, canonical)|=0.879 < 0.90, OR clause). The hierarchy-weighted density recipe produces zero task-type discrimination across all tested alpha values (0.1, 0.3, 0.5) with identical mean density (0.667) across listing, detail, and cart page types. The recipe is a perfect monotonic reparameterization of area-weighted density (Spearman rho=1.0 at alpha=0.3) because the depth estimation heuristic uses inForm (binary flag) rather than actual DOM tree structure, making the depth distribution task-invariant. Hull-breaking on 7/21 pairs is entirely ISOLATED-A-LINK and definition-dependent, not task-type-dependent. Positive control PC1 fails (inter-type ratio=1.0). Null control NC1 fails (random weights show equivalent correlation structure). Audit PASS confirms all recomputed metrics match producer; audit VF-1 identifies depth estimation as heuristic (not true DOM depth); audit VF-2 corrects producer p-values (irrelevant to binary decision rule). The negative result is bounded to heuristic depth estimation on truncated-first-20 locatable_sample (7 tasks, 1 Magento site, 3 definitions); true DOM tree depth with parent-child links remains untested (producer U-1).

claim_updates.reason: Hierarchy-weighted density (exp(-alpha*depth) with 4-level inForm/tag heuristic, alpha=0.1/0.3/0.5) on truncated-first-20 locatable_sample produces zero task-type structure (eta-squared=0.0 at all alphas, PC1 ratio=1.0), is a perfect monotonic reparameterization of area-weighted density (Spearman rho=1.0 at alpha=0.3), and fails to provide a viable third recipe for MIXED outcome resolution. Positive control PC1 fails (all type_means=0.667, inter-type ratio=1.0). Null control NC1 fails (random weights equivalent to hierarchy). Hull-breaking is definition-dependent (100% ISOLATED-A-LINK), not task-type-dependent. Bounded to heuristic depth estimation on truncated-first-20 sample; true DOM tree depth untested.

product_action: NONE — The MIXED outcome program remains without a validated third recipe. No viable density-based MIXED decision rule exists among canonical, weighted, linear mean, density ratio, or hierarchy-weighted approaches. The 31x canonical/weighted material gap is established but unusable for MIXED classification. Product lane should restrict density metric use to recipe-insensitive task-definition pairs only, pending either true DOM tree depth testing or abandonment of density-based MIXED handling.
next_question: Would TRUE DOM tree depth (actual parent-child distances from <html>, 2-20+ levels, from complete DOM with preserved hierarchy, not the 4-level inForm heuristic on a flattened 20-element sample) produce eta-squared > 0.10 and rho(weighted) < 0.90 with hierarchy-weighted density breaking the convex hull in a task-type-dependent way?
reason: The heuristic hierarchy recipe is falsified as a MIXED decision rule: it provides zero task-type discrimination (eta-squared=0.0) and is a monotonic reparameterization of weighted density. However, the negative result is strictly bounded to the heuristic depth estimation (audit VF-1, VF-4). The root cause is that inForm-based depth is binary and task-invariant across the fixed 20-element locatable_sample. True DOM tree depth could vary by page type (listing pages have deeper nesting than cart pages) and could produce a structurally different recipe. The open question is whether genuine DOM hierarchy information — not available in the truncated flattened sample — can break the 2-recipe degeneracy. This is blocked by runtime lane (full-DOM capture with preserved hierarchy). If true DOM depth also fails, the MIXED outcome program should be abandoned and density-based handling restricted to recipe-insensitive pairs.
